problem: Autoregressive image generation suffers from high latency due to slow sequential patch-by-patch generation, limiting practical deployment.
approach: Introduces flexible parallelized autoregressive modeling with learnable position query tokens to enable multi-patch generation at once, combined with locality-aware generation ordering that groups patches to minimize dependencies.
contribution: Reduces generation steps from 256 to 20 for 256x256 resolution and 1024 to 48 for 512x512 resolution with 3.4x lower latency while maintaining quality.

problem: The precise mechanism and effects of classifier-free guidance in masked discrete diffusion models remain theoretically unclear.
approach: Provides exact analytical characterization of guidance in low-dimensional discrete diffusion by quantifying how guidance amplifies class-specific regions while suppressing shared regions, deriving distribution-free dynamics.
contribution: Shows that guidance strength induces distinct covariance structures and exhibits double-exponential decay rates in total variation, with quantitatively different behaviors in 1D versus 2D.

problem: Running large 30-70B LLMs on consumer hardware with limited CPU/GPU, insufficient memory, and slow storage remains impractical.
approach: Proposes pipelined-ring parallelism to overlap disk I/O with compute, introduces Halda heterogeneity-aware scheduler for per-device workload optimization, and implements mmap-based offloading to handle mixed CPU/GPU resources.
contribution: Achieves 674ms/token on 70B model with less than 6% memory pressure and 26 tokens/s on 32B with speculative decoding, 5-17x faster than prior systems.

problem: Multimodal collaborative perception systems fail catastrophically when key sensors like LiDAR become unavailable due to semantic mismatches from feature fusion.
approach: Proposes length-adaptive multimodal fusion (LAMMA) that adaptively handles missing modalities while maintaining semantic consistency, combined with a pretrain-align-fuse training strategy to preserve modality-specific features.
contribution: Enables systems to maintain optimal performance across all individual modalities even when specific sensors fail, addressing modality competition issues.

problem: Vision-language models struggle with real-world clinical reasoning requiring analysis of multiple images with cross-view evidence fusion and diagnosis synthesis.
approach: Introduces MedThinkVQA benchmark with 8,481 expert-annotated cases averaging 6.51 images per case, requiring stepwise supervised reasoning across multiple views.
contribution: Benchmarks show GPT-4o achieves 57.39% accuracy and reveals that 70% of errors stem from image reading and cross-view integration failures.

problem: Large language models fail to systematically generalize to novel compositions of known geometric transformations in abstract spatial reasoning tasks.
approach: Introduces Compositional-ARC dataset testing generalization from known transformations (translation, rotation) to novel combinations, evaluates meta-learning approaches designed for compositionality.
contribution: A 5.7M-parameter meta-learned transformer outperforms state-of-the-art LLMs like GPT-4o and Gemini 2.0 Flash on compositional spatial reasoning.

problem: End-to-end speech-text models either generate discrete speech tokens independently without text awareness or suffer from computational overhead and frequency mismatches with standard approaches.
approach: Proposes DrVoice with dual-resolution speech representations reducing input frequency from 12.5Hz to 5Hz via joint autoregressive modeling, enabling mutual modality awareness.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art on OpenAudioBench, VoiceBench, and UltraEval-Audio benchmarks as a leading 7B open-source speech foundation model.

problem: Speech synthesis faces a fundamental trade-off where discrete tokens ensure stability but sacrifice expressivity, while continuous signals retain richness but suffer from error accumulation.
approach: Introduces hierarchical semantic-acoustic modeling with semi-discrete residual representations: a text-semantic language model generates plans while a residual acoustic model recovers fine-grained details via end-to-end diffusion.
contribution: Trained on 1 million hours of speech, achieves state-of-the-art zero-shot TTS among open-source systems without requiring external discrete speech tokenizers.

problem: Concept Embedding Models fail to represent inter-concept relationships and require concept annotations at multiple granularities, limiting practical interpretability applications.
approach: Proposes Hierarchical Concept Embedding Models (HiCEMs) that explicitly model concept hierarchies, introduces Concept Splitting to automatically discover sub-concepts from embeddings without additional annotations.
contribution: Enables fine-grained explanations from limited labels and supports powerful test-time concept interventions at different granularities, improving task accuracy.

problem: Evaluating model-level explanations for GNNs is limited to class score metrics, which are insufficient to assess whether explanations truly represent the classifier's reasoning.
approach: Introduces sufficiency risk as a formal evaluation criterion and derives distribution-free certificates bounding this risk, develops Coverage, GGA, and Overlap metrics with finite-sample concentration bounds.
contribution: Provides the first theoretically certified framework for evaluating GNN explanations, revealing explanation quality differences hidden by class scores alone.

problem: Modeling marked temporal point processes requires training specialized models for each target system, making it data-intensive and inflexible for new domains.
approach: Proposes Foundation Inference Model for Point Processes (FIM-PP) using amortized inference and in-context learning: pretrains on synthetic Hawkes processes to infer conditional intensity functions in-context.
contribution: Matches specialized models on next-event prediction without additional training and enables rapid finetuning on real-world data.

problem: Aligning discrete diffusion models with rewards typically applies rewards to final outputs and backpropagates globally, leading to computational inefficiency and incompatibility with arbitrary rewards.
approach: Proposes stepwise decomposition that decomposes trajectory alignment into per-step posterior matching objectives, maintaining compatibility with arbitrary rewards while enabling efficient optimization.
contribution: Achieves 12% improvement in predicted activity on DNA sequence design and improves GSM8K from 78.6 to 81.2 on LLaDA-8B, with 12% improvement on multiple domains.

problem: Traditional image generation approaches lack fine-grained control over the generation process across multiple levels of visual detail.
approach: Introduces Next Visual Granularity (NVG) generation that decomposes images into sequences of visual granularities at same spatial resolution but varying token vocabulary, progressively refining from layout to details.
contribution: Outperforms VAR baseline with FID scores of 2.06 vs 2.09 on ImageNet and shows clear scaling behavior.

problem: Multi-view graph domain adaptation must mitigate domain shift while accounting for structural information across multiple views and different neighborhood levels.
approach: Proposes Structural Aggregation Guided Alignment (SAGA) with Structural Aggregation Distance (SAD) metric that jointly considers view and neighborhood order, enabling dynamic selection of dominant view-order pairs.
contribution: Effectively characterizes and mitigates both view-level and hop-level structural discrepancies through dynamic alignment.

problem: Knowledge distillation between language models with different tokenizers requires computing likelihood ratios but fails when vocabularies differ.
approach: Leverages the recursive structure of Byte-Pair Encoding to create a probabilistic framework for cross-tokenizer likelihood scoring, providing exact computation for subset vocabularies.
contribution: Achieves up to 12% reduction in memory footprint for Qwen2.5-1.5B and 4% performance improvement on distillation tasks, with 2% improvement on GSM8K reasoning.

problem: Video object segmentation in complex scenarios with appearance variations and dynamic scene transformations requires high-level conceptual reasoning beyond feature matching.
approach: Proposes Segment Concept (SeC) framework using Large Vision-Language Models to construct robust conceptual priors across frames, injecting concept-level features when new scenes appear.
contribution: Achieves 11.8-point improvement over SAM 2.1 on the new SeCVOS benchmark designed for semantic complexity.

problem: Reliable certification of LLMs with imperfect judges is challenging because judge noise and bias invalidate statistical guarantees.
approach: Introduces Noisy but Valid hypothesis testing framework using small calibration set to estimate judge's TPR/FPR, derives variance-corrected threshold for large judge-labelled dataset.
contribution: Provides finite-sample Type-I error control despite calibration uncertainty, with first systematic treatment of imperfect-judge evaluation.

problem: Monitoring LLM API consistency over time is expensive with existing audit methods, leaving model updates largely unmonitored.
approach: Proposes cost-effective continuous monitoring using LLM log probabilities (logprobs) as a statistical marker, requesting only single token output.
contribution: Detects changes as small as one fine-tuning step while being 1000x cheaper than existing methods.

problem: Vision-language models suffer from affirmative bias, failing to understand negation correctly in described object detection tasks.
approach: Proposes CoVAND dataset with systematic chain-of-thought pipeline and NegToMe token merging module that binds negation tokens with attributes into coherent semantic phrases.
contribution: Improves NMS-AP by up to 10.8 points on OVDEval with lowered false positive rates and generalizes to state-of-the-art VLMs.

problem: Multi-agent systems fail when deployed due to model mismatches from environment uncertainties, but existing robust methods require simulators or large offline datasets.
approach: Proposes MORNAVI algorithm for online learning in Distributionally Robust Markov Games, using only environmental interactions without prior data.
contribution: Achieves low regret and efficiently finds optimal robust policies for TV and KL divergence uncertainty sets.

problem: Text-to-image models generate visually appealing images that fail to match semantic content of user descriptions due to prompt engineering neglecting semantic alignment.
approach: Proposes VisualPrompter, a training-free framework with self-reflection module identifying absent concepts and target-specific optimization that refines prompts at atomic semantic level.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on multiple text-image alignment benchmarks with plug-and-play compatibility.

problem: How functional behaviors emerge from heterogeneous synaptic plasticity mechanisms remains poorly understood, limiting biological neural network modeling.
approach: Harnesses Darwinian evolutionary principles to discover biologically plausible heterogeneous plasticity rules in realistic visual cortex model, parameterizing spikes, traces, and neuromodulation.
contribution: Uncovers diverse high-performing plasticity rule families achieving similar outcomes with different formulations, suggesting computational degeneracy in synaptic learning.

problem: Reward models in RLHF are susceptible to length bias exploitation, and fine-tuned LLMs struggle to adhere to explicit length instructions.
approach: Proposes Response-conditioned Bradley-Terry model explicitly differentiating semantic preferences from length requirements, introduces Rc-RM and Rc-DPO algorithms.
contribution: Improves length bias mitigation and instruction following across models and datasets while maintaining semantic preference quality.

problem: LLM-based agents for EHR database access face challenges from vague user questions and terminology mismatches with database entries, but no benchmarks evaluate this real-world workflow.
approach: Introduces EHR-ChatQA benchmark evaluating end-to-end agent workflow with query clarification, value matching, and SQL generation across two interaction flows: IncreQA and AdaptQA.
contribution: Shows high Pass@5 (90-95% and 60-80%) but substantially lower Pass^5 (35-60%), highlighting consistency challenges in safety-critical settings.

problem: Deepfake detection lacks large-scale unified training resources and massively pre-trained models despite numerous benchmarks.
approach: Introduces MMI-DD dataset with 3.6 million facial images, fine-grained annotations across four deepfake types, and VLM descriptions; proposes SD2 method using CLIP-based image-text classification.
contribution: Constructs foundational deepfake knowledge space with type-specific labels and contrastive learning, enabling effective generalization to AIGC benchmarks.

problem: Modern LLMs cannot faithfully communicate their internal answer distributions, instead adding percentage numbers or hedging words to single responses.
approach: Develops SelfReflect metric using information-theoretic distance to measure faithfulness between LLM's uncertainty summary and actual answer distribution.
contribution: Shows LLMs are incapable of revealing uncertainties through reasoning or finetuning alone, but can generate faithful summaries when sampling outputs and feeding back into context.

problem: Existing RL datasets are orders of magnitude smaller and less diverse than web-scale pretraining corpora, creating a data bottleneck for scaling RL.
approach: Introduces Webscale-RL pipeline that systematically converts large pretraining documents into diverse, verifiable question-answer pairs, creates dataset of 1.2 million examples across 9 domains.
contribution: Achieves performance of continual pretraining with 100x fewer tokens through more efficient RL training.

problem: Autoformulation of sequential decision-making problems like Markov decision processes is challenging due to large formulation space and complexity of interpreting optimal policies.
approach: Proposes operator-theoretic autoformulation using LLMs to construct Bellman equation as graph of interpretable operators, applies customized Monte Carlo tree search with solver feedback.
contribution: Proves universal three-level operator-graph topology that significantly shrinks MDP formulation search space, enabling practical autoformulation for queueing systems.

problem: Acquiring pose priors for object categories is difficult, yet priors effectively improve pose estimation.
approach: Proposes Pose Prior Learner (PPL) using hierarchical memory to store compositional prototypical poses, distills general pose prior from which template transformation and reconstruction improve estimation.
contribution: Learns meaningful pose priors without annotations, outperforms baselines on human and animal pose estimation, and effectively handles occluded images.

problem: Adversarial Imitation Learning is considered unstable, with reward assignment functions typically derived from divergence objectives without considering their impact on dynamics.
approach: Uses LLM-guided evolutionary framework to discover data-driven reward assignment functions based on imitation policy performance, yields DAIL meta-learnt AIL algorithm.
contribution: Discovered reward assignment functions generalize across unseen environments and optimization algorithms, outperforming human-designed baselines with more stable training.

problem: Comprehensive benchmarks for evaluating Deep Research Agents that conduct multi-step research and synthesis are absent.
approach: Introduces DeepResearch Bench with 100 PhD-level research tasks crafted by domain experts across 22 fields, proposes automated reference-based and citation-based evaluation methods.
contribution: Provides automated evaluation methodologies highly aligned with expert judgments, enabling systematic assessment of DRA research quality and information retrieval.

problem: Offline domain randomization requires fitting simulator parameter distributions to offline data, but theoretical foundations for when this approach is sound remain unexplored.
approach: Casts offline domain randomization as maximum-likelihood estimation over parametric simulator families, provides statistical guarantees with weak and strong consistency under regularity conditions.
contribution: Establishes principled theoretical foundations for ODR under identifiability assumptions and clarifies when offline data can guide randomization distributions.

problem: Supervised fine-tuning of foundation models often leads to poor generalization where prior capabilities deteriorate after tuning on specific tasks.
approach: Proposes Proximal SFT incorporating trust-region constraints from TRPO/PPO, stabilizes optimization by viewing SFT as policy gradient with constant positive advantages.
contribution: Matches standard SFT in-domain while outperforming on out-of-domain generalization, remains stable under prolonged training without entropy collapse.

problem: Joint audio-video generation requires synchronized, semantically aligned sound and vision, but existing open-source methods lag commercial models in quality and synchrony.
approach: Proposes JavisDiT++ with modality-specific mixture-of-experts for cross-modal interaction, introduces temporal-aligned RoPE for frame-level synchronization and audio-video direct preference optimization.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on 1M public training entries, significantly outperforming prior approaches in quality, consistency, and synchrony.

problem: Random variate generation is a computational and energy bottleneck in probabilistic machine learning despite its central importance.
approach: Introduces scalable sampling strategy using efficient lookup tables with fast index sampling for arbitrary distributions, achieves near-optimal entropy cost.
contribution: Achieves 40% time and 60% energy savings compared to state-of-the-art, 100x improvement over common Python samplers.

problem: Diffusion Transformers use constant patch size across timesteps, limiting sampling efficiency despite high-noise timesteps requiring fewer visual details.
approach: Introduces Pyramidal Patchification Flow (PPFlow) using larger patches at high-noise timesteps and smaller patches at low-noise timesteps, shares transformer blocks across timesteps.
contribution: Achieves 2.02x denoising speedup on SiT-XL/2 and 1.61-1.86x on FLUX.1 text-to-image with comparable quality.

problem: Diffusion models for decision-making achieve strong results but suffer from slow inference speed, limiting practical deployment.
approach: Proposes consistency distillation for offline RL that directly incorporates reward optimization into distillation via decoupled training and noise-free reward signals.
contribution: Achieves 9.7% improvement over state-of-the-art and 142x speedup over diffusion models in inference time.

problem: Differential privacy noise interacts with optimizer adaptivity in complex ways, requiring better understanding for practical high-privacy settings.
approach: Analyzes private optimizers through stochastic differential equations lens, compares DP-SGD and DP-SignSGD under fixed and optimal hyperparameters.
contribution: Shows adaptive methods dominate in high-privacy regimes with epsilon-independent optimal learning rates, making them far more practical.

problem: Active perception is crucial in robotics with sparse sensors like touch, but current methods are task-specific with limited generality.
approach: Proposes APPLE framework that jointly trains transformer-based perception module with RL-based policy using unified optimization, generalizable across tasks.
contribution: Achieves high accuracies on Tactile MNIST and other tasks, demonstrating versatility as general framework for active perception.

problem: Multimodal large language models with code generation abilities remain limited despite success in visual-textual understanding.
approach: Proposes VisCodex using task vector-based model merging to integrate coding LLM into vision-language backbone, introduces Multimodal Coding Dataset of 598k samples and InfiBench-V benchmark.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art among open-source MLLMs approaching proprietary models like GPT-4o on visually-rich programming tasks.
